label: TP
reason: Alert 1 (xss) is FP: The sink at L68-L70 writes to response.getWriter(), but the variable fileName is wrapped in ESAPI.encodeForHTML(), which escapes HTML special characters, rendering XSS payloads harmless. Alert 2 (path-injection) is TP: The sink at L63 constructs fileName by concatenating a hardcoded directory with 'bar', which resolves to the raw user input from the header (verified by ternary calc: 188 > 200 is false, so bar=param). No path traversal validation occurs, allowing attackers to escape the base directory.

evidence.note: User input retrieved from header and assigned to param; ternary logic ensures bar=param
Path injection sink: fileName constructed from user-controlled bar without validation
XSS sink: fileName is encoded via ESAPI.encodeForHTML before output
